name: Triple Operations
title: E. Triple Operations
legend:
On the board Ivy wrote down all integers from l to r, inclusive.

In an operation, she does the following:

pick two numbers x and y on the board, erase them, and in their place write the numbers 3x and ⌊
y


3
⌋. (Here ⌊∙⌋ denotes rounding down to the nearest integer).

What is the minimum number of operations Ivy needs to make all numbers on the board equal 0? We have a proof that this is always possible.
input_spec:
The first line contains an integer t (1≤t≤104) — the number of test cases.

The only line of each test case contains two integers l and r (1≤l<r≤2⋅105).
output_spec: For each test case, output a single integer — the minimum number of operations needed to make all numbers on the board equal 0.
note:
In the first test case, we can perform 5 operations as follows:
1,2,3
→


x=1,y=2
3,0,3
→


x=0,y=3
1,0,3
→


x=0,y=3
1,0,1
→


x=0,y=1
0,0,1
→


x=0,y=1
0,0,0.
